The discussions are expected to focus on strategic trade resilience, cross-border payment mechanisms, energy security, and conflict-resolution pathways regarding ongoing geopolitical tensions in Eastern Europe and West Asia.

items.title: States are using a roundabout way to borrow. And that's raising concerns
items.summary: Borrowing through special purpose vehicles and state corporations creates an illusion of fiscal prudence, while putting the state government on the hook for potentially paying interest and principal.

items.title: India ramps up domestic LPG production as renewed US-Iran attacks spark fresh fears over Strait of Hormuz supplies
items.summary: India is increasing domestic cooking gas production to address supply gaps. Local refiners aim to add over ten percent to current output levels. Imports through the Strait of Hormuz are now less reliable due to renewed attacks. Domestic consumption has also significantly decreased since the war began. This shift helps meet demand while mitigating import risks.

items.title: 6.2 mbd: Saudi Arabia reports lowest oil exports since 1990
items.summary: Saudi Arabia's crude oil output significantly dropped last month to its lowest point since 1990. Renewed hostilities between the United States and Iran impacted the kingdom's export routes. This production slump illustrates the fallout of the prolonged Iran conflict on West Asia energy producers. Saudi crude exports also fell by about a third in August, according to data. items.title: Oil surges 6%, Brent and US crude both surpass $100 on more tanker attacks
items.summary: Oil prices climbed over one hundred dollars per barrel on Thursday amid escalating attacks on shipping lanes. The surge was driven by fears of supply disruptions sparked by the Houthis' capture of a Yemeni port, posing significant risks to Red Sea navigation. Market analysts suggest that China's oil buying habits will be pivotal in determining the trajectory of future prices.
